title: Restricted-mode posting for sensitive incidents (minimal in #incidents, full bundle in restricted channel)
author: Jacob Stein
description:
Problem: During higher-severity incidents we sometimes paste context bundles that contain customer-identifying metadata (request IDs, tenant IDs, internal resource names) into #incidents threads. Even with redaction, responders have asked for a stricter mode that limits what lands in broadly visible channels while still making the full bundle available to the on-call / incident commanders.

This PR adds “restricted mode” posting behavior:

- When an incident is flagged as restricted, the bot posts a minimal message in the public incident thread (#incidents): incident id, start time, affected service/region, and links to dashboards/runbook + a pointer to the restricted channel thread.
- The bot posts the full context bundle (deploy/config/saturation collectors) in a restricted Slack channel (default: #incidents-restricted) with the same incident thread structure.
- Adds configuration knobs (channel allowlist + restricted channel id) and a per-incident override so IC can request restricted posting without redeploy.
- Adds an audit log entry for every restricted-mode post attempt (success/failure, collectors included, redaction mode, destinations).

Guardrails:
- Fail-open: if restricted channel posting fails, bot still posts minimal metadata to #incidents plus an explicit “restricted bundle failed to post” status line with a retry hint.
- Redaction still applies in restricted channel (restricted != unredacted); restricted just changes visibility and reduces blast radius.
- Rate limiting is preserved (shared limiter across both destinations).

Config:
- INCIDENT_BOT_ALLOWED_CHANNELS: comma-separated allowlist for public posting.
- INCIDENT_BOT_RESTRICTED_CHANNEL: channel id/name for restricted bundle.
- INCIDENT_BOT_RESTRICTED_TRIGGERS: list of signals we treat as restricted by default (e.g., incident label “customer_sensitive”, pagerduty severity P0 + customer tag) (can be disabled).

Docs:
- Adds on-call docs describing when to use restricted mode, what data is still prohibited (payloads/tokens), and how to request a restricted bundle from the bot.

Testing:
- Unit tests for routing + failure modes (restricted channel missing perms, restricted channel posting timeout).
- Local smoke test using Slack sandbox workspace + mock incident payload.

Refs: ENG-2847 (posting controls), ENG-2845 (hardening), INT-1188 (verbosity + safe posting concerns).

conversation: Sean Gallagher (review): This is the right direction. Two asks: (1) Make sure the public thread explicitly says where the full bundle was posted (channel + permalink), and (2) Can we ensure we never include customer identifiers in the public minimal post? Even tenant name should not show up. Right now you include "account" when present.

Jacob Stein (author): Good catch. Updated minimal payload to only include incident id, service, region, severity, and timestamps. Removed any account/tenant fields. Also added explicit "Full context bundle posted in <#incidents-restricted>" with permalink when available; otherwise falls back to channel mention + timestamp.

Marcus Lin (security review): Restricted channel is not an excuse to relax redaction. Please document this clearly and add an audit record that indicates whether restricted mode was used and which destinations were attempted. Also: what happens if the bot lacks permission to post in the restricted channel?

Jacob Stein (author): Agree. Added docs section "Restricted != unredacted" + added audit event `restricted_mode_post` with destination statuses and redaction mode. For missing perms / post failure, we fail-open by still posting minimal metadata to #incidents with a status line noting restricted bundle failed and including the audit event id + retry hint. We do NOT fall back to posting the full bundle in #incidents.

Rafael Mendes (review): Please ensure we don't create thread spam across both channels on retries. I see retries happen per collector; in restricted mode, retries could double. Can we gate retries behind a single bundle-level attempt or cache the bundle for a window?

Jacob Stein (author): I changed retry behavior: bundle assembly is unchanged, but Slack posting now has a single bundle-level retry (max 1) and uses a deterministic message key (incident_id + window_start + window_end) to avoid duplicates. Collector retries remain internal; Slack posting duplicates are deduped via the message key stored in memory for 15m. (Follow-up: caching across restarts is out of scope here.)
Chloe Martin (review): The config names are fine but please align with our other bot env var naming. Also docs should mention how IC sets restricted mode (label? slash command?).

Jacob Stein (author): Renamed vars to `INCIDENT_BOT_ALLOWED_CHANNELS` / `INCIDENT_BOT_RESTRICTED_CHANNEL` and added doc snippet for `@incident-bot restrict on` / `@incident-bot restrict off` (implemented as incident thread command that toggles an in-memory override for the incident id; it times out after 6h).
Marcus Lin (security): One more: add a safety check so the restricted channel cannot be set to #incidents (or any allowlisted public channel). This prevents misconfig.
Jacob Stein (author): Added validation in config loader: restricted channel must not be in allowed public channels list; startup fails with clear error if misconfigured.

Rafael Mendes (approval): LGTM. This gives us an on-call usable default and satisfies the security guardrails. Please make sure we announce to #eng-sre once merged with the new command + channel policy.
Sean Gallagher (approval): Approved. Thanks for removing account fields from the minimal public post; that was the main concern.
